supervisor.name: open_lane
supervisor.description: Open a lane for one outcome: creates its branch and working copy and starts a Lead there with this directive. One lane per independent outcome.

outcome.description: The observable change and what you assumed, in a few sentences (under 800 characters). Decisions go in acceptance and outOfScope.

acceptance.description: Checks that show the outcome done, including the decisions you made, one per item.

appetite.description: What the outcome is worth, as a budget.

deadline.description: When to cut scope and keep going, or none.

issue.description: Optional GitHub issue: #12, owner/repo#12 or a URL.

base.description: Optional base branch; defaults to the project's.

supervisor.name: message
supervisor.description: Send a Lead (by lane id) or, for a recovery, a Peer (by task id) one message. It is delivered when the recipient's turn ends; a message to a Peer is copied to its Lead.

supervisor.name: answer
supervisor.description: Answer an open ask by its id. The asker gets the answer when idle and the ask closes.

supervisor.name: close_lane
supervisor.description: Close a lane and archive its agents. With land true the desk lands the lane branch on the base branch: a fast-forward, or a merge in the main working copy when the base moved; if that is not possible the reason comes back and the branch stays for the Human.

supervisor.name: set_project
supervisor.description: Set this project's base branch and gate: the command that proves the lane works (for example npm test). By default it runs once on the whole lane, when its Lead reports it ready and before it lands, so tasks merge into the lane without each having to build on its own.

gateOn.description: lane (default): run the gate when a lane is reported ready and before landing. task: also run it on every task merge.

supervisor.name: status
supervisor.description: The current status of every lane, task and open ask in this project.

lead.name: start_task
lead.description: Start a Peer on one task in its own branch and working copy, off your lane branch. Default to one task for the whole lane; add another only when its write set is independent and it can run in parallel, and say why in context. A task never needs to build on its own. The brief is built from these fields.

acceptance.description: Behaviors that show the task done; each needs one focused check.

owned.description: Exact paths the Peer may change.

context.description: Decisions made, approaches ruled out, where to start reading.

lead.name: start_review
lead.description: Start a read-only reviewer with clean context. With task: it reviews that task's branch. Without task: it answers the open question on your lane branch, which is how a council seat, a scout or an audit reader starts.

task.description: Optional task id whose branch is reviewed.

focus.description: The open question for the reviewer, asked neutrally, with any output format it must follow.

title.description: Optional short name, at most 60 characters.

lead.name: message
lead.description: Send one of your Peers (by task id) a message. It is delivered when the Peer's turn ends; a running Peer is never interrupted.

lead.name: answer
lead.description: Answer a Peer's open ask by its id.

lead.name: accept
lead.description: Accept a finished task: its branch merges into your lane branch. A task does not have to build or pass tests on its own; the gate runs on the whole lane when you report it ready.

lead.name: rework
lead.description: Send a task back to its Peer with what must change.

lead.name: cut
lead.description: Cut a task or finish with a reviewer: its agent stops and its branch is not merged.

lead.name: ask
lead.description: Ask the owner. need: a resource or decision from above. blocked: something outside the project stops you. question: user-visible behavior the directive leaves open. Give your default and keep working on it unless the step can't be undone.

lead.name: report
lead.description: Report the lane to the owner: when it is ready to land, when it is cut, or when a decision above you changed. At most 15 lines.

ready.description: True when the lane branch holds the whole outcome. The desk runs the gate on the lane branch first and refuses the report if it fails.

lead.name: status
lead.description: The current status of your lane's tasks and open asks.

peer.name: done
peer.description: Hand the task back. Call it once at the end of the task, after committing on your branch.

summary.description: What changed and why, in a few lines.

checks.description: Commands run and their real results.

discovered.description: Problems found outside the task, including a premise that turned out wrong.

peer.name: ask
peer.description: Ask whoever assigned the task, when you cannot continue without an answer. End your turn after asking; the answer arrives as a message.

tried.description: What you checked and your best guess.

reviewer.name: done
reviewer.description: Hand the review back. Call it once at the end.

findings.description: One finding per paragraph: severity P0-P3, file:line, the failure, the smallest fix.

reviewer.name: ask
reviewer.description: Ask whoever assigned the review, when you cannot continue without an answer.
